answer: A concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is proof-of-unique-work with stake bonding: every agent must lock collateral before it can vote or attest, and its influence decays unless peers re-verify its identity each epoch. Picture a raven patrolling a frozen tundra - it costs energy to stay aloft, and a flock of clones drains the same food supply, so duplicates become unprofitable fast. New agents board like a slow voyage: reputation accrues only through costly, verifiable service over time, never through cheap key creation, making mass-registered sybils economically doomed.
